`tests/**` was never type-checked (vitest transpiles without checking), so turning the
compiler on reports 562 errors across 114 of 307 files — and 193 files are already clean,
which is what makes a ratchet worth more than a one-shot cleanup: a NEW test file is
checked from the day it is written, while the backlog is cleared per-slice.
Removing an entry is the whole point. `scripts/typecheck-tests.mjs` fails when an entry
here has become clean, so the removal cannot be forgotten in the commit that earned it,
and it fails when an entry names a file that no longer exists, so a rename cannot smuggle
one back on. Adding an entry is a decision to be argued for in review, not a way past red.
